question.problem:
$\,$ $P(x):$ $x\in N$ $\,$ $Q(x):$ $x\in Z$

Consider the predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ above. Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x)⇒Q(x)?$

I. If $x\in Z,$ then $x\in N$

II. $x\in Z$ if $x\in N$

III. $x\in N$ implies $x\in Z$

IV. $x\in N$ only if $x\in Z$

current_example.problem:
Consider the following predicates:

$\qquad$ $P(x):$ $x$ is prime $\qquad$ $Q(x):$ $x$ is not a multiple of $10$

Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)?$

I. $x$ is not a multiple of $10$ if $x$ is prime

II. If $x$ is not a multiple of $10,$ then $x$ is prime

III. $x$ is prime implies $x$ is not a multiple of $10$

IV. $x$ is not a multiple of $10$ only if $x$ is prime
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's recall the following grammatical constructions for the implication $P\Rightarrow Q{:}$

- If $P,$ then $Q$

- $P$ only if $Q$

- $Q$ if $P$

- $P$ implies $Q$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

- Option I reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272126/assets/d1608fdb6351f5f1c2d1eb3638d06b0ea78bf3f32454274db0c198dfaf52154a.svg)
which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{green}\checkmark}$

- Option II reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272126/assets/78c39e66bcd7055e9749b13d5b40a87f2a1612c74736ca3a3c641fcbc46ccd46.svg)
which corresponds to $Q(x) \Rightarrow P(x).$ $\:{\color{red}\times}$

- Option III reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272126/assets/916d44c5e66c3b5ff0b9f6d962efc2c083b45244ccadc115d0913f79582f2d10.svg)
which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{darkgreen}\checkmark}$

- Option IV reads
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272126/assets/5a4aba0723bfffa5b004ba28bd38008057d87079715fc2fc921e566f99d9dbda.svg)
which corresponds to $Q(x) \Rightarrow P(x).$ $\:{\color{red}\times}$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
